name: Canonical ownership map
title: Audit {subject} canonical ownership and extension seams
scope: Map the existing runtime owners, contracts, configs, tests, and public extension seams for {subject}. Reuse the canonical owner; do not invent a parallel service or state path.
acceptance: The ticket produces a source-backed owner map and identifies exactly where future variants should extend the current architecture.

name: Contract consistency
title: Verify {subject} contracts match current runtime consumers
scope: Trace shared contracts/config through server and client consumers for {subject}; remove stale assumptions only when source evidence proves drift.
acceptance: All active consumers agree on stable IDs, field shapes, ownership, and failure semantics; focused source audits prevent contract drift.

name: Lifecycle startup
title: Harden {subject} startup ordering and partial-dependency behavior
scope: Audit startup order, initialization prerequisites, and partial construction paths for {subject}; fail/bound safely rather than stalling the ordered bootstrap.
acceptance: Startup is bounded and deterministic under missing/late dependencies, with a focused regression fixture for the discovered dependency boundary.

name: Intent/input validation
title: Reject malformed or untrusted inputs at the {subject} authority boundary
scope: Enumerate player/client/external intents that reach {subject}; validate identity, shape, bounds, ownership, and current state on the server or canonical owner.
acceptance: Malformed, stale, replayed, out-of-range, or unauthorized intents fail closed without changing authoritative state.

name: State normalization
title: Normalize {subject} state into one canonical representation
scope: Audit duplicate/legacy state shapes around {subject}; centralize normalization at an existing owner/resolver instead of adding another source of truth.
acceptance: One canonical normalized state is used across active paths and tests cover malformed/legacy inputs without silent divergence.

name: Deterministic resolution
title: Extract or verify deterministic resolution for {subject}
scope: Move repeatable gameplay/pipeline decisions for {subject} into pure deterministic resolvers where practical, while keeping Roblox adapters thin.
acceptance: Same inputs produce the same outputs, edge cases are executable outside Studio where appropriate, and runtime adapters do not duplicate the resolver logic.

name: Failure fallback
title: Define bounded fallback behavior for {subject} failures
scope: Identify recoverable dependency/runtime failures in {subject} and define explicit bounded fallbacks that preserve authority and avoid soft-locks.
acceptance: Each named recoverable failure has an observable fallback or explicit stop reason; no infinite retry or silent authority bypass remains.

name: Bounded waits
title: Bound every dependency wait and retry loop in {subject}
scope: Audit WaitForChild/network/bootstrap/retry loops around {subject}; apply bounded waits/retries and explicit failure handling consistent with the current lifecycle.
acceptance: No production path in the scoped owner can wait/retry indefinitely on a dependency; source audit/regression coverage locks the bound.

name: Teardown cleanup
title: Make {subject} teardown and replay lifecycle-clean
scope: Audit disconnect, stop, destroy, replay, and reinitialization for {subject}; remove listeners/tasks/state that can leak across runs or players.
acceptance: Repeated start/stop/replay leaves no duplicate listeners, timers, state owners, or orphaned instances in repository-level tests.

name: Reconnect/resume
title: Specify reconnect or resume behavior for {subject}
scope: Trace what state may survive a client reconnect, server handoff, or run return for {subject}; preserve only server-owned/durable identity and rebuild presentation safely.
acceptance: Reconnect/resume cannot duplicate rewards/actions or trust client-restored state, and the expected restoration boundary is covered by tests or explicit deferral.

name: Concurrency/contention
title: Stress {subject} under simultaneous players/runs
scope: Exercise the canonical owner for {subject} with multiple players, squads, enemies, or run instances as applicable; identify accidental singleton or shared-state coupling.
acceptance: Independent actors cannot overwrite each other's state; bounded capacity/fairness rules are deterministic and tested where the system supports concurrency.

name: Idempotency/replay defense
title: Make {subject} mutations idempotent against duplicate delivery
scope: Audit mutations/events/requests in {subject} for retries and duplicate delivery; use stable IDs or canonical state checks where value or progression could be repeated.
acceptance: Duplicate/replayed accepted operations do not double-apply damage, rewards, inventory, progression, session ownership, or lifecycle transitions.

name: Observability
title: Add actionable observability for {subject}
scope: Expose bounded structured diagnostics for key state transitions, failures, and capacity limits in {subject} without leaking sensitive/player-private data.
acceptance: A developer can distinguish success, rejection, timeout, capacity, stale-state, and dependency failure classes from repository/runtime evidence.

name: Failure reason taxonomy
title: Standardize failure reasons emitted by {subject}
scope: Replace ambiguous booleans/free-form branches in the scoped {subject} boundary with stable reason identifiers where consumers/tests need to react.
acceptance: Failure reasons are stable, documented by tests, and do not expose exploitable internal details to untrusted clients.

name: Configuration validation
title: Validate authored configuration for {subject}
scope: Add or strengthen fail-fast validation for IDs, references, numeric bounds, incompatible combinations, and missing content used by {subject}.
acceptance: Invalid authored data fails validation before play/runtime mutation; valid existing content remains compatible.

name: Extension seam
title: Create the next low-cost extension seam for {subject}
scope: Identify the repeated shape most likely to grow in {subject}; extend an existing registry/config/resolver seam so the next variant is data-driven instead of copied code.
acceptance: At least one future variant can be added through the canonical extension point without duplicating core authority or lifecycle code.

name: Cross-system integration
title: Verify {subject} integrates through canonical neighboring owners
scope: Trace upstream/downstream handoffs for {subject}; remove direct cross-layer shortcuts and use existing public APIs/contracts where available.
acceptance: Integration tests/source audits prove each authoritative mutation crosses the intended owner boundary exactly once.

name: Authority/source audit
title: Add a source audit that forbids a second owner for {subject}
scope: Create or strengthen a repository source audit around {subject} to catch untrusted client authority, duplicate authoritative state, forbidden generated-source edits, or legacy parallel paths.
acceptance: The audit fails on a representative forbidden regression and passes on the canonical architecture.

name: Focused regression suite
title: Expand focused executable regression coverage for {subject}
scope: Add high-value deterministic fixtures for success, boundary, malformed, stale, and cleanup cases in {subject}; prefer pure/domain tests where possible.
acceptance: The focused suite covers the highest-consequence invariants and would fail if the scoped bug/contract class returned.

name: Integration acceptance
title: Add an end-to-end source/integration acceptance for {subject}
scope: Create a bounded integration fixture/source audit proving the canonical config → shared contract → server owner → client/presentation or downstream handoff for {subject}.
acceptance: The acceptance test proves the intended wiring exists and rejects a missing, duplicated, or bypassed integration path.

name: Performance budget
title: Set and enforce a performance budget for {subject}
scope: Identify the dominant CPU/memory/network/pathfinding/instance cost for {subject}; add deterministic budget checks or instrumentation where repository testing can enforce it.
acceptance: The scoped system has an explicit capacity/budget target, bounded degradation behavior, and evidence hooks for Studio-only profiling when required.

name: Consumer/readability boundary
title: Audit player-facing readability of {subject} without moving authority client-side
scope: Review the presentation/consumer boundary for {subject}: timing, state visibility, failure feedback, input affordance, and clutter. Keep all authoritative outcomes server-owned.
acceptance: Players receive timely, non-misleading feedback for authoritative states, and presentation failure cannot mutate or fabricate gameplay state.

name: Studio evidence packet
title: Define the minimum Studio evidence packet for {subject}
scope: List only engine/device facts for {subject} that cannot be truthfully proven by repository validation, including exact setup, seeds/players/devices, observations, and failure triggers.
acceptance: Source-complete work can be marked BUILT — VERIFICATION PENDING, and VERIFIED requires the named evidence rather than vague manual testing.

name: Coverage & leverage registry
title: Reconcile {subject} with coverage and efficiency registries
scope: Run development-coverage/efficiency tooling for {subject}; update mappings only when a coherent change materially moves coverage or creates/retires a reusable capability.
acceptance: Coverage metadata points to canonical owners/evidence and does not overstate VERIFIED runtime behavior; leverage notes identify real reusable seams only.

name: Exit gate & rollout
title: Define the capability exit gate and rollback trigger for {subject}
scope: Write/encode the smallest measurable exit gate for the scoped {subject} capability, including validation tier, pending Studio facts, rollback trigger, and downstream unlock.
acceptance: The coordinator can tell when the capability is source-complete, when it is VERIFIED, what would force rollback, and which dependent work becomes eligible.
